draft.title: Evidence for moving continents
card: Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents move slowly over time. His idea was called continental drift. Later evidence from the sea floor turned it into the theory of plate tectonics.
Wegener noticed that the coastlines of South America and Africa fit together like puzzle pieces. He also found similar fossils and rock types on continents now far apart across oceans.
Marie Tharp mapped the ocean floor and showed a long ridge with a rift valley down its centre. This fits with new crust forming where plates move apart.
Rock on the sea floor records Earth's magnetic field as it forms. It shows matching stripes on both sides of a ridge, which suggests new rock forms at the ridge and spreads outwards.
draft.remember: Wegener's land clues came first. Later sea-floor evidence showed the plates move.

a.q: Wegener found the same kind of land animal fossil in South America and Africa. What did he propose from this?
opts: The continents were once joined, then drifted apart
The animal swam across the ocean to breed
The continents have always been in their present places
The fossils were formed by rock stripes on the sea floor
a.why: A land animal could not cross a wide ocean, so Wegener proposed that the continents were once joined and have drifted apart. Swimming across is a tempting idea, but the card says the fossils are found on continents now far apart across oceans.
a.clue: Think about where a land animal could live.

b.q: Matching magnetic stripes are found in sea-floor rock on both sides of a ridge. What does this later evidence suggest?
opts: New rock forms at the ridge and spreads outwards
Old rock is sinking at the ridge and being destroyed
The coastlines on each side fit together like a puzzle
The ridge was mapped by Marie Tharp using fossils
b.why: The rock records Earth's magnetic field as it forms, so matching stripes on both sides suggest new rock forms at the ridge and spreads outwards. The puzzle fit is one of Wegener's clues, but it comes from coastlines, not from magnetic stripes.
b.clue: The rock records the magnetic field as it forms.

a.best: The continents were once joined, then drifted apart

b.best: New rock forms at the ridge and spreads outwards
